No, but it's going to significantly reshape the job landscape in ways we're still figuring out.

Some jobs will definitely be displaced - particularly those involving routine information processing or pattern recognition that AI can do faster and cheaper. Other jobs will be augmented rather than replaced - think doctors using AI diagnostic tools, or programmers using AI assistants. And new categories of work will emerge that we can't fully anticipate yet.

The jobs most resistant to replacement tend to involve physical manipulation in unpredictable environments, complex human interaction and judgment, or creative work where the value is in the distinctly human perspective. But even here, the boundaries keep shifting as the technology improves.

The bigger uncertainty isn't really "will AI replace *all* jobs" (almost certainly not) but rather how quickly displacement happens, whether we create new jobs fast enough, and how we handle the economic transition. Those are partly technical questions but mostly social and political ones.

What's driving your question - are you thinking about your own career, or more generally curious about the economic impacts?
